title: Bitcoin Reaches Eight-Month High After Clarity Act Loss
title_cn: Bitcoin Reaches Eight-Month High After Clarity Act Loss
summary:
Bloomberg Intelligence Senior US Policy Analyst Nathan Dean discusses the Securities and Exchange Commission giving the green light for digital versions of securities to start trading in the US. This plan could reshape traditional market structure after crypto legislation failed a key Senate vote on Tuesday.

Also affecting the crypto space, Bitcoin surged past $85,000 to its highest since late-January, extending a sharp rebound as falling oil prices and a broader return of risk appetite helped cryptocurrencies move past setbacks on US crypto legislation and monetary policy. The original cryptocurrency climbed as much as 6.5% to $86,331 in New York trading, almost $10,000 above the lows touched last week after the Clarity Act stalled and the Federal Reserve raised interest rates. Even after that rebound, Bitcoin remains roughly a third below its record last October. Nathan Dean speaks with Bloomberg's Joe Mathieu on Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)

summary: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA), Vice Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, says he opposes a diesel export ban, but warns US oil producers against using higher global prices to boost profits while creating scarcity at home. Frank Cilluffo, Director of the McCrary Institute for Cyber and Critical Infrastructure Security at Auburn University, says the US will “never firewall” its way out of the cyber threat and needs to take more proactive steps against adversaries. summary: Frank Cilluffo, Director of the McCrary Institute for Cyber and Critical Infrastructure Security at Auburn University, says the US will “never firewall” its way out of the cyber threat and needs to take more proactive steps against adversaries. Cilluffo says AI can strengthen defenders but warns that, for the foreseeable future, the initiative remains with attackers. Cilluffo also argues the US must keep human control over increasingly powerful AI systems while continuing to compete with China. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Rep. Issa Warns Oil Companies Against Profiting From US Shortage

summary: Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA), Vice Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, says he opposes a diesel export ban, but warns US oil producers against using higher global prices to boost profits while creating scarcity at home. Rep. Issa calls the gains a “tremendous windfall,” and companies “can’t have it both ways.” Rep. Issa argues the US has mismanaged the Houthi threat for years, allowing the group to rebuild its capabilities and support attacks in the region. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
